text.p: Ashland Inc Monday reported a profit of $2.97 per share for the year ended September 30 saying it was a reasonable year despite a very hostile competitive environment for the refining business.
Three businesses -- Ashland Chemical, APAC highway construction operations and Valvoline -- achieved all-time record earnings in fiscal 1996," the company said.
"We're very pleased by their performance and also by significant improvement from Ashland Exploration and Arch Mineral Corporation."

Rapidly rising crude oil prices led to severe margin compression and a weak fourth quarter for Ashland Petroleum, the company said. For the fiscal year, operating income totaled $55 million, "a disappointing result" that included profit of only $8 million in the final quarter.
The unit earned $50 million in fiscal year 1995 before charges that left it with a loss of $54 million.

Refinery runs averaged nearly 369,000 barrels a day, up 5 percent from 1995, Ashland said. In addition, 485 retail locations were open and operating by September 30, compared to 80 last year, under the revitalized Ashland marketing program.
These improvements, however, were offset by higher average crude oil costs, which could not be fully passed through in product prices, the company said.

A competitive retail environment also affected results from SuperAmerica, it continued. Operating income declined to $34 million, from 1995's $53 million, reflecting retail gasoline margin compression. Sales of gasoline and merchandise both increased, reflecting the addition of 38 stores.

Results from coal operations were mixed. Arch Mineral had its best year since 1990. Ashland Coal had a difficult year due largely to the effects of announced contract expirations. "For the most part, our results for 1996 can be summed up this way: We formulated a plan, and we carried it through," chief executive Paul Chellgren said. "We said we would increase capital employed in chemicals, construction, and a few other areas, and we have. This increase was rewarded with record results and excellent returns highlighted by a 25 percent return on capital employed from APAC.

"Consequently, we will continue to pursue growth opportunities in our related energy and chemical businesses. Equally important, we must realize improved returns from our petroleum refining and gasoline marketing businesses."
